findings.description: False positive: CodeQL flagged a type annotation field as hardcoded credentials
findings.code_snippet: password: str | None\n    \"\"\"The password part of this host, or `None`.\"\"\"
findings.reasoning: This is a false positive. Line 141 contains a type annotation for a field named 'password' in a TypedDict class definition. There is no actual hardcoded password value - it's simply declaring that the field can hold a string or None. The docstring is documentation explaining what the field represents. The CodeQL detector appears to have a pattern matching issue where it flags any mention of 'password' in field definitions, even when no actual secret is hardcoded. This is a legitimate data structure definition used to represent URL components in the pydantic_core library.

evidence.code_context: This is part of the MultiHostHost TypedDict class definition which represents components of a multi-host URL. The class has fields for username, password, host, and port - all of which are optional (str | None or int | None). No actual values are assigned to these fields.
evidence.dataflow_analysis: No data flow exists here - this is a type definition, not executable code that assigns values. The 'password' identifier is purely a field name in a data structure definition.
evidence.notes: The CodeQL hardcoded-credentials query appears to have a false positive pattern where it flags field names containing 'password' in docstrings, even when no actual hardcoded value exists. This is a common pattern in security scanning tools where they over-match on keywords without understanding the context.
